svg.title: The authorities' path
svg.desc: An imagery plate of John 9-10. A road winds from the foreground to a hill on the horizon. 1, beside the road in the foreground, Moses' seat: a stone chair with a carved back, left empty, the scroll of the Law lying on it: 'The scribes and the Pharisees sit on Moses' seat' (Matthew 23:2); 'gods to whom the word of God came' (John 10:35). 2, five authorities walk the road away from the seat, backs to the reader, mantles with woven stripes and tassels over their heads, stones in their hands, one stone raised: 'And they reviled him' (John 9:28); 'The Jews picked up stones again to stone him' (John 10:31). 3, in the background a synagogue, its door dark, and the healed man standing outside it: 'You were born in utter sin, and would you teach us?' And they cast him out (John 9:34). 4, in the foreground off the road, Jesus stands with His back to the reader, and the man He healed kneels before Him with his hands raised, in a soft light: he 'washed and came back seeing' (John 9:7); 'If this man were not from God, he could do nothing' (John 9:33); 'Lord, I believe,' and he worshiped him (John 9:38). 5, the far road runs into darkness: 'They have neither knowledge nor understanding, they walk about in darkness' (Psalm 82:5); 'now that you say, We see, your guilt remains' (John 9:41). 6, where the road ends, a pair of scales stands on the hill under a darkening sky: 'nevertheless, like men you shall die, and fall like any prince' (Psalm 82:7); 'Arise, O God, judge the earth' (Psalm 82:8). Across the foot: 'For judgment I came into this world, that those who do not see may see, and those who see may become blind' (John 9:39).
